chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad al-Warraq, who said:

I presented to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) a book containing a Quran that was sealed and studded with gold, and the end of the chapter was written in gold. I showed it to him, and he did not find fault with anything in it except the writing of the Quran in gold, for he said: 'I do not like that the Quran be written except in black, as it was written the first time.'

key_terms.مُعَشَّرٌ: studded or adorned (with gems or gold)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on writing the Quran in gold ink according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the distinction between the validity of Quranic manuscripts and the recommended etiquette (adab) of their presentation. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the use of gold embellishments but specifically prefers black ink for the text itself, emphasizing a return to the simplicity and authenticity of the initial compilation (mushaf) over ostentatious decoration. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the purity of the text while allowing for aesthetic variations in physical copies.
